summary: Iterate over every regex match while keeping capture groups and match positions.
documentation: matchAll returns an iterator of match arrays, each containing the full match, capture groups and its UTF-16 index. Materializing that iterator lets a parser return structured occurrences instead of only matching text.
inputs: A string containing zero or more double-braced placeholders. Valid names consist of one or more lowercase ASCII letters.
returns: An ordered list of objects with name and index for each valid placeholder occurrence.
caution: A RegExp passed here must have the g flag. Matches are non-overlapping, and index is a UTF-16 offset rather than a user-perceived character count. Regex matching is not a complete template-language parser.
scenarios: List editable placeholders in a local message-template preview.
Highlight every supported token with its source position.
Detect repeated field references before exporting a template.
title: Locate every supported placeholder
problem: Find all non-overlapping substrings matching /\{\{([a-z]+)\}\}/g. Return {name, index} for each, in source order. Keep repeated names; ignore uppercase, numeric and empty names. Use UTF-16 match offsets.
hint: Spread matchAll into an array and map each match to its first capture and index.
goal: Use String.matchAll() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
